history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Jain temple (Svetambara), keep-or-drop decision needed. The Neminath shrine stands INSIDE the main Ranakpur Jain temple campus, a stone's throw from the Chaumukha temple and near the Sun temple. A small, compact Nagara-style shrine, described as a replica of the nearby Parshwanath temple: raised platform (jagati) reached by steps, open-pillared mandapa, small antarala, garbhagriha with a shikhara of subsidiary urushringa spires. Dedicated to Neminatha, the 22nd Tirthankara (believed a contemporary of Krishna and to have attained moksha at Girnar). DISTINCT from the Neminath temple at Girnar (seq 1506, id neminath-jain-temple) - this is the Ranakpur shrine only, and NOT a duplicate of 2185/the Chaumukha temple.

name: Neminath Temple, Ranakpur
town_description: Ranakpur is a village in Pali district, Rajasthan, in a secluded Aravalli valley about 90 km from Udaipur. It is home to the celebrated 15th-century Jain temple complex (the Chaumukha/Adinath temple and satellite shrines including Neminath, Parshwanath, Surya and Amba), one of the five holiest Jain pilgrimage sites, in the Gorwad Panch Tirth circuit.

travel.road: Inside the Ranakpur Jain Temple complex on SH-32, about 93 km from Udaipur; walkable from the main Chaumukha temple.
